papers.title_in_file: Quantum computational sensing using quantum signal processing, quantum neural networks, and Hamiltonian engineering
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I. Introduction, VI. Discussion and Outlook; the body sections and appendices were not read in full
papers.what_it_is: Theory and simulation of quantum computational sensing protocols (quantum signal processing, quantum neural networks, bosonic Hamiltonian engineering) for classification tasks in sensing.

assertions.value: The authors report, in theory and numerical simulation, a regime in which a quantum computational sensor reaches higher accuracy than a conventional quantum sensor for a given sensing-time budget, with a simulated accuracy advantage of >20 percentage points for some tasks.
quotes: we have been able to show a regime of operation where a quantum computational sensor can achieve higher accuracy than a conventional quantum sensor for a given budget of sensing time, with a simulated accuracy advantage of >20 percentage points for some tasks
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulation study; the figure is a simulated advantage over the authors' chosen baseline.
assertions.reader_inference: The advantage is against a conventional quantum sensor baseline defined by the authors, not against a classical ML model on classical hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that their analyses used unitary models of quantum evolution (up to measurement), and that the effect of experimental imperfections on the protocols has yet to be evaluated.
quotes: Our analyses in this paper used unitary models of quantum evolution (up to measurement).
It is an open question, for each protocol, to what extent the advantage of QCS over conventional QS can be maintained under realistic experimental conditions.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own modelling scope and open question in the Discussion (VI.B), pp.19-20.

assertions.value: The authors state that in their simulation studies the parameter optimization used gradient descent with the assumption of access to the exact gradient.
quotes: in our simulation studies we have performed the parameter optimization using gradient descent where it has been assumed that we have access to the exact gradient.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Discussion (VI.B), p.19.

papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks for Classification and Data Compression Tasks
papers.what_it_is: Simulation benchmark of QCNNs against a hardware-efficient ansatz for phase classification of Ising and XXZ ground states and for quantum autoencoder compression.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in simulation, QCNN with RY gates can be trained faster because it has fewer trainable parameters while matching the performance of hardware-efficient ansatz models.
quotes: The results show that QCNN with RY gates can be trained faster due to fewer trainable parameters while matching the performance of HEAs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single simulation study on two model families.
assertions.reader_inference: Table I lists a best HEA (3 layers) test accuracy slightly above the best QCNN (RY); the paper's own numbers show matching, not a win on accuracy.

assertions.value: The authors state that they examined system sizes of 4, 8, and 16 qubits through simulation, on the ground states of the transverse field Ising model and the XXZ model.
quotes: Various system sizes, including 4, 8, and 16 qubits, through simulation were examined.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the abstract, p.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that the simulation results will subsequently be compared against implementation on hardware, and that the choice of classical optimizer significantly impacts training efficiency and final model performance.
quotes: The simulation results obtained will subsequently be compared against implementation on hardware using the Qibolab software library
The choice of classical optimizer significantly impacts the training efficiency and final model performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion (IV), p.2: results are simulation only.

papers.title_in_file: Implementing a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network by Utilizing a Variational Quantum Circuit for Detection of Dementia
papers.what_it_is: Single-author study adding a variational quantum circuit layer to ResNet-18 for binary dementia classification of Kaggle MRI images.

assertions.value: The authors report that the hybrid QCCNN provided 97.5% and 95.1% testing and validation accuracies, against 91.5% and 89.2% for the classical network.
quotes: This study found that the proposed hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural network (QCCNN) provided 97.5% and 95.1% testing and validation accuracies, respectively, which was considerably higher than the classical neural network (CNN) testing and validation accuracies of 91.5% and 89.2%.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study, one public Kaggle dataset, one run reported.
assertions.reader_inference: Table II lists 0.975 and 0.915 as training accuracy and 0.965 and 0.900 as testing accuracy, which does not match the abstract's labels.

assertions.value: The authors report that on a testing set of 100 normal and 100 dementia MRI images the QCCNN classified normal and demented images correctly 95% and 98% of the time, against 89% and 91% for the CNN.
quotes: using a testing set of 100 normal and 100 dementia MRI images, the QCCNN detected normal and demented images correctly 95% and 98% of the time, compared to the CNN accuracies of 89% and 91%
assertions.certainty_reason: Single 200-image test set.

assertions.value: The authors state that the hybrid model's better predictions are due to its inherent quantum nature, which they describe as another example of quantum supremacy.
quotes: The proposed hybrid model provides better predictions than the original ResNet-18 model due to its inherent quantum nature, which displays another example of quantum supremacy
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' assertion; no experiment isolates a quantum cause.
assertions.reader_inference: The run shows a gap on one dataset; it does not show quantum supremacy or isolate the quantum layer as the cause. No simulator or hardware is named.

assertions.value: The authors state that, if run on a remote quantum computer with enough qubits, the model could potentially run faster and require less feature space than its classical counterpart.
quotes: if ran on a remote quantum computer with enough qubits, this proposed model could potentially run faster and require less feature space than its classical counterpart
assertions.certainty_reason: Speculation stated in the Conclusion.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no run on quantum hardware.

papers.title_in_file: Realizing Stabilized Landing for Computation-Limited Reusable Rockets: A Quantum Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I. Introduction, state/action/reward setup, V. Performance Evaluation, VI. Conclusions
papers.what_it_is: Quantum reinforcement learning applied to a simulated rocket-landing task (OpenAI Gym Lunar-Lander), compared with DQN and actor-critic.

assertions.value: The authors report that the proposed QRL algorithm has the smallest number of training parameters, with normalized ratios 4.29 and 3.77 times smaller than DQN and actor-critic.
quotes: The normalized ratios of numbers of parameters in the proposed algorithm are 4.29 and 3.77 times smaller than DQN and actor-critic.
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulated environment.

assertions.value: The authors report that the proposed algorithm increases the reward the fastest and obtains the highest convergence reward among the compared algorithms.
quotes: the proposed algorithm increases the reward the fastest and obtains the highest convergence reward
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulated environment; no repeated-run statistics stated in the text read.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experimental environment is Lunar-Lander from OpenAI Gym, with 4 qubits, Pauli-Z measurement and X-rotation gates.
quotes: The experimental environment is Lunar-Lander provided by Open AI gym.
the number of qubits used for training, measurement, and gate are 4, Pauli-Z, and X-rotations, respectively
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup in V, p.5.
assertions.reader_inference: The evaluation is a game-physics simulation, not a real rocket and not quantum hardware.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I. Introduction, V.A scaling studies, Table II, VI. Conclusion; remaining ablations and supplementary material not read in full
papers.what_it_is: IonQ hybrid architecture adding a parameterized quantum circuit head to a SetFit sentence transformer for SST2 sentiment classification, in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report up to 3.14% improvement in accuracy over classical architectures of comparable model size, within the set of hyperparameters probed in the study.
quotes: We observe up to 3.14% improvements in accuracy over classical architectures of comparable model size, within the set of hyperparameters probed in this study.
assertions.certainty_reason: Screening study; simulation; comparison is to a classical model of comparable parameter count.
assertions.reader_inference: The 3.14% figure compares the best quantum model with the best classical model of comparable size (an SVC); neural-network baselines in Table II with many more parameters score within about 1 point of the quantum models.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the single-encoder architecture accuracy shows an upward trend as the number of qubits increases, with the result at 18 qubits going against that trend, which they attribute to the fixed hyperparameters.
quotes: In the single-encoder architecture, accuracy shows an upward trend as the number of qubits increases
the observed accuracy at 18 qubits goes against the this trend, an artifact we attribute to fixing the particular reupload number
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation sweep at fixed other hyperparameters.

assertions.value: The authors state that their studies use finite shot-counts and noisy-gate simulations, and list as future work full fine-tuning with the base language model weights unfrozen and validation on physical quantum hardware.
quotes: Our studies are based on finite shot-counts and include simulations based on noisy quantum gates.
One direction for future work is to perform full fine-tuning by unfreezing the weights of the base language model.
Finally, we plan to validate our findings by performing inference and training on physical quantum hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of scope and future work in the Abstract and VI.

assertions.value: The authors report that increasing the re-upload number, main block layers and re-uploading layers does not directly enhance accuracy, and that increasing the number of qubits is a more effective strategy.
quotes: we observe that increasing re-upload number, number of main block layers, and number of re-uploading layers does not directly enhance accuracy.
we deduce that increasing the number of qubits is a more effective strategy to improve the accuracy of the model.
assertions.certainty_reason: Screening study over a limited hyperparameter set.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, 1 Introduction, 12 Future work; the theorem proofs were not read
papers.what_it_is: Mathematical study of continuous quantum walks on weighted join graphs: strong cospectrality, periodicity and perfect state transfer.

assertions.value: The paper proves that, under certain conditions, there are graphs with no perfect state transfer that exhibit it when joined by another graph, which the authors say suggests the join operation is promising for producing new graphs with PST.
quotes: Under certain conditions, we show that there are graphs with no PST that exhibits PST when joined by another graph.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a proved result in the abstract; the individual theorem was not located in this read.

assertions.value: The paper proves a bound on the transition-matrix entries of the join graph relative to those of X, valid for adjacency and Laplacian Hamiltonians, and shows the bound is tight for infinite families of graphs.
quotes: While the join operation need not preserve periodicity and PST, we show that
tight for infinite families of graphs
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract, p.1, and the introduction cite Corollary 73 for the bound; the bound's formula is in the abstract in math notation.
assertions.reader_inference: The bound itself is a math expression garbled in the text extraction, so the value does not restate it.

assertions.value: The authors conjecture that Laplacian perfect state transfer does not occur in a simple connected unweighted graph on an odd number of vertices.
quotes: If X is a simple connected unweighted graph on an odd number of vertices, then Laplacian perfect state transfer does not occur in X.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conjecture 77, stated as an open problem without proof.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Amplitude Amplification for Solving QUBO Problems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I. Introduction, VI. introduction, VIII. Conclusion; sections II to V read only through the introduction and conclusion summaries
papers.what_it_is: Classical-simulation study of gate-based amplitude amplification with phase-encoded cost oracles for QUBO problems, with a variational choice of one scalar parameter.

assertions.value: The authors state that, unlike Grover's oracle, using the cost oracle Uc achieves peak measurement probabilities only up to 70-90%, while using the same iteration count as standard Grover's.
quotes: using Uc is only able to achieve peak measurement probabilities up to 70-90%
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Introduction; the measurement is from classical simulation of random QUBOs.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithm is not applicable to any QUBO blindly: depending on the solution-space distribution it may be impossible for amplitude amplification to find one extremum or the other.
quotes: Depending on how the numerical values of a given problem form a solution space distribution, it may simply be impossible for amplitude amplification to find one extrema or the other.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' stated limit in the Conclusion (VIII).

assertions.value: The authors state that the section V results were found through classical simulations of quantum systems, that a remaining challenge is finding the correct ps value, and that how quickly the needed information can be produced experimentally is an open question.
quotes: The results of section V. were all features of amplitude amplification using Uc that were found through classical simulations of quantum systems.
a different challenge lies in finding the correct ps value to use in order to boost these states.
is exactly how quickly quantum can find the optimal solution, which is an open question for further research.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of scope and open question in I, VI and VIII.
assertions.reader_inference: Section VI, the variational algorithm, is described by the authors as primarily speculative.

papers.title_in_file: AutoQML: Automated Quantum Machine Learning for Wi-Fi Integrated Sensing and Communications
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I. Introduction, II.A experiment setup, III results and analysis, IV. Conclusion
papers.what_it_is: MERL proof-of-concept using Bayesian-optimization ansatz search (AutoAnsatz) for a quantum neural network on Wi-Fi human pose recognition data.

assertions.value: The authors report that the best QNN found by AutoQML, a 3-layer MPS ansatz on 10 qubits with angle embedding and 54 variational parameters, outperforms the state-of-the-art DNN model that has 650-fold more trainable parameters (35,000).
quotes: After AutoQML exploration, the best ansatz was chosen with 3-layer MPS for 10-qubit and angle embedding, having 54 variational parameters.
The best MPS model outperforms the state-of-the-art DNN model which has 650-fold more trainable parameters (i.e., 35,000).
assertions.certainty_reason: One in-house experiment; test accuracy values are in a figure.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper does not say whether a real quantum processor was used; the conclusion defers real-processor validation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiment used 8 poses, with the measurements of the first four sessions as training data and the last three as testing data, giving 42,915 training and 1,040 testing samples.
quotes: The subject is asked to perform a total of 8 poses
We use the measurements in the first four sessions as a training data and those in the last three sessions as a testing data.
The total number of measurement samples is 42,915 and 1,040 in the training and testing, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own data setup in II.A, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that validation on real quantum processors will be provided in future work and describe the study as a very initial proof-of-concept.
quotes: Validation on real quantum processors will be provided in a future work.
This is a very initial proof-of-concept study for quantum-ready Wi-Fi sensing
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit in the Conclusion (IV), p.4.
